houseViews.view: Maintained: the freeze holds and remains stratified. Sydney Northwest is still the pure strike — 33 months of stock, only 191 of 570 listings priced (34%), asking $2,410/m² against $2,342 on the thin priced tail. Sydney Southwest asks $2,107 vs $1,511/m² certified (+39% gap) at 28.7 months, while Sydney South West has converged to honest pricing ($2,196 vs $2,084, a 5% gap) yet still carries 33.7 months on just 264 annual sales — proof that at $725k medians, honest pricing alone doesn't clear a market this deep. NSW's headline improvement (16.5→15.3 months over 30 days) is denominator and mix, not basin repricing.
houseViews.falsifier: Basin priced-share rising above 60% (Northwest especially) alongside corridor months-stock falling below 20 on rising sold counts.

houseViews.view: Maintained: VIC is the only major market where the overhang is still building — 16.9→17.1 months over 30 days with actives up 6,368→6,572 — but it remains the only deep market that is honestly priced: 95% of listings carry a price and the ask-to-sold gap is a workable 13% ($841 vs $742/m²) versus Sydney's up-to-39%. Cheap ($394k), abundant, and screenable keeps VIC the mechanical landing zone for the late-2026 investor rotation; the fringe corridors (Melbourne North 20.9 months on 488 sales, Northwest 16.1 on 532) are digesting, not frozen, and the overhang caps price growth rather than volume.
houseViews.falsifier: VIC months-stock pushing past 20 with sold 12m rolling below ~4,000, or new-listing absorption failing to lift by Q1 2027.

houseViews.view: Maintained: the true VIC distress sits an hour past the fringe — Melbourne Peri-Urban at 38.5 months on just 125 annual sales, South Gippsland 33.1 on 100, Gippsland 26.2 on 66, West Gippsland 20.8 on 144. These are demand deserts, not merely overpriced markets: ask-to-sold gaps run 13–25% ($576 asked vs $508 sold in Peri-Urban, $628 vs $504 in South Gippsland), and with metro fringe lots at $394k and 17 months of choice there is no scarcity premium left for the 644–772m² lifestyle lot further out. Avoid englobo and stage stock across the belt; this clears last.
houseViews.falsifier: Belt sold volumes rising 50%+ per window, or peri-urban months-stock falling below 25 without listings simply being withdrawn.

houseViews.market: Regional VIC hubs vs the fallen-angel prints (Ballarat/Bendigo)
houseViews.view: New: trust the corridor, not the 7-sale suburb print. Bendigo appears atop the fallen angels at -37.6% last 12m — but on 7 sales with lot sizes simultaneously down 37%, a mix artefact — while the Bendigo corridor clears 304 annual sales at 8.8 months and Ballarat clears 458 at 10.1 months, both tighter than the VIC state figure of 17.1. Mechanism: at $320–325k medians these hubs are the cheapest functioning volume markets in the state, absorbing the affordability-priced buyer VIC's fringe can't serve at $410–440k. The genuine regional weakness is the low-volume satellites (Creswick -36.8% 3yr on 8 sales, Smythesdale -22.2% on 5), not the hubs.
houseViews.falsifier: Ballarat/Bendigo corridor months-stock rising above 14 or corridor sold $/m² printing negative on stable 250+ sale windows.

houseViews.view: Maintained: capitulation clears — Torquay's decline is decelerating (-13.5% prior year → -5.9% last 12m) with volume at 43 sales in the latest window versus 9 three years ago; Winchelsea cut -11.8% and printed 21 sales. Contrast Portarlington (-27.3% over 3yrs on 10 sales) and San Remo (-25.9% on 15) where vendors still hold 2022 rates and the adjustment is incomplete. The bottom in the priced, cutting coastal names is forming; the holdouts have another leg down.
houseViews.falsifier: Torquay/coastal volumes falling back below ~15 per window, or price declines re-accelerating past -10% in the next windows.

houseViews.view: Maintained with rising conviction: sold base +10% in 30 days (10,069→11,070) while months-stock fell 13.7→13.4 into a 7% listings build (11,497→12,337) is exactly the early-positioning footprint ahead of the 1 Jul 2027 changes (negative gearing narrowed to new builds, CGT discount replaced by indexation). The bid lands where product is priced and cheap — VIC (95% priced, $394k), outer QLD and SA — not Sydney basins where 66% of Northwest stock cannot even be screened. Tight markets (SA 6.2 months, WA 7.9, Adelaide North 5.4) get the price inflation; loose priced markets get the volume.
houseViews.falsifier: No pickup in investor-share of land sales or VIC/QLD new-listing absorption by Q1 2027, or policy amendment before commencement.

houseViews.view: Maintained: tightness is genuine — 6.2 months statewide, Adelaide North clearing at ask ($914 asking vs $910 sold $/m², 5.4 months), a zero-negotiation market — but the headline ~28% sold-$/m² growth remains composition-inflated (one estate ≈ a third of 2026 sales; like-for-like ≈ +9.5%). The $420k median in the historically cheap state is defended almost entirely via lot compression (Roseworthy -47% lot size over 3yrs, Mount Barker -27%, Morphett Vale -33%) — compression is the market's confession that the gross-price ceiling binds. While stock holds near 6 months the path is deceleration, not correction, and the 2027 rotation delays the reckoning.
houseViews.falsifier: Stock above 10 months, incentive share rising two runs in a row, or lot compression stalling while sales volumes fall.

houseViews.view: Maintained at high conviction: $/m² accelerating into the ceiling — +49.7% then +99.6% to $1,027/m² (vs $344 three years ago) while lots compressed another 38% in one year and volume thinned 79→45→35 sales per window. A market doubling its rate while shrinking the product a third on falling volume is borrowing from the price ceiling, not raising it. Sell stage stock into this rate; do not underwrite englobo at $1,027/m² residuals.
houseViews.falsifier: Lot sizes stabilising while $/m² keeps rising on volume recovering above ~50 sales per window.

houseViews.market: Thin-volume rocketships (Greenbank QLD, Virginia SA) + WA collision
houseViews.view: Updated — merging the WA view into the hazard class it belongs with. The unpriceable prints persist: Greenbank +56.6% to $1,373/m² on 6 sales (down from 76 three years ago), Virginia +72.9% to $1,120 on 8 (from 48) — sell-out selection, not demand; treat any window under ~15 sales as noise, versus Mount Barker's real +61% on 90 sales. WA itself is the same late-cycle shape at state scale: listings +21% in 30 days (607→732, the largest build of any state) into a still-tight 7.9 months, vendors asking $1,041 against $867/m² sold (a 20% forward-priced gap), Mandurah accelerating (+24.4%→+98.6%, lots -35% 3yr) while Hilbert and Australind fade (59→27%, 53→43% second derivatives). Developers rushing stock while vendors price the next leg is how tight markets end.
houseViews.falsifier: WA months-stock rising above 10; or Greenbank/Virginia volumes recovering above ~20 per window with $/m² holding, converting the prints to genuine repricing.

houseViews.view: Maintained: the state series remains contaminated by the 7-Jul universe expansion (948→1,022 suburbs) — the 30-day 'crash' (asking $539k→$478k, $/m² $1,029→$710, actives 758→1,056) is regional QLD (Townsville $305k at 8.8 months, Gympie, Kingaroy) entering the sample, not repricing. Corridor and suburb evidence says the underlying market is firm at 8.9 months statewide: South Ripley +82% last 12m to $1,774/m² on 33-sale windows, Bahrs Scrub +53% to $1,319/m² on stable 16–23 sale windows. Screen QLD at corridor level until the new-suburb history matures.
houseViews.falsifier: Like-for-like (pre-expansion suburb set) QLD asking or sold $/m² actually falling on the next monthly comparison.
